rgb-color-codes.quickAnswer: This is a searchable reference of 24 common colors with exact codes. Tomato, for example, is #FF6347 - RGB(255, 99, 71): full red, 99 green, 71 blue. Type any name or HEX fragment in the search box to filter the chart, then tap to copy the HEX.
keyFacts: Every color here uses its standard web (CSS) definition - the same values browsers use.
HEX and RGB describe the identical color; #FF0000 and rgb(255, 0, 0) are the same red.
Primary web colors are red, lime and blue; secondaries are yellow, cyan and magenta.
Searching matches the color name in your language and the HEX code.
All 24 codes are safe to paste directly into CSS, HTML or design tools.
howTo: Type a color name (like 'teal') or HEX fragment (like 'FF6') in the search box.
The chart filters instantly to matching colors.
Read the HEX and RGB values beside each swatch.
Tap the copy button on any row to copy its HEX code.
Clear the search to see the full chart again.
rgb-color-codes.formula:
No computation here - this is a reference table.
Example entry: Tomato = #FF6347.
Split the HEX pairs: FF -> 255, 63 -> 99, 47 -> 71.
So Tomato = RGB(255, 99, 71).
rgb-color-codes.workedExample:
Looking up Tomato:
1. Type 'tom' in the search box; the chart filters to Tomato.
2. Read the row: swatch, name, #FF6347, RGB(255, 99, 71).
3. Verify: 0xFF = 255 (full red), 0x63 = 99, 0x47 = 71.
4. Tap copy: #FF6347 is now on your clipboard, ready for CSS.
5. Use it as color: tomato; in CSS or #FF6347 anywhere a HEX is accepted.
benefits: Faster than guessing HEX codes from memory.
Search works in English, Hindi and Arabic color names.
One-tap copy puts the exact code on your clipboard.
Standard web values - what you copy is what the browser renders.
limitations: Only 24 common colors; rare or brand-specific colors are not listed.
Names follow web conventions, which sometimes differ from paint or print names.
Values assume sRGB, the web standard.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HEX and RGB?
faqs.a: Nothing in meaning - they are two notations for the same 24-bit color. #FF6347 and rgb(255, 99, 71) describe the identical tomato red. HEX is compact; RGB is readable.

faqs.q: Are these the same colors CSS uses?
faqs.a: Yes. Named web colors like 'tomato', 'teal' and 'coral' are CSS standards, and the HEX values here match the browser definitions exactly.

faqs.q: Why is web green #008000 but lime #00FF00?
faqs.a: Historical CSS naming: 'green' was defined as the darker #008000, while the full-intensity #00FF00 got the name 'lime'. This chart lists lime for the pure primary.

faqs.q: Can I search in Hindi or Arabic?
faqs.a: Yes - the search matches color names in the language you are browsing in, plus HEX fragments in any language.

faqs.q: How do I use a copied code in CSS?
faqs.a: Paste it as a value: color: #FF6347; or background: rgb(255, 99, 71);. Both work in any stylesheet.
These are the most-looked-up reference colors. For any other color, use the channel or picker tools to get exact codes for arbitrary colors.
